findings.description: `MergeLockLostError` is declared inline in `merge-gate.service.ts`, next to `withMergeLock`, which throws it. `general.md` (lines 37-38) says: "**No inline error classes.** An `Error` subclass is declared in the area's `errors/` folder, never beside the code that throws it." The sibling `MergeLockHeldError` already lives in `src/core/merge-gate.errors.ts`, so that file is the natural home.
findings.body:
This PR adds `MergeLockLostError` inside `merge-gate.service.ts`, right next to `withMergeLock`, the function that throws it:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/e9684760009548da6f7471c54729f37972c3baac/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L842-L862

Two conventions say error classes don't go there:

- `docs/conventions/general.md` §Structure (lines 37-38): "**No inline error classes.** An `Error` subclass is declared in the area's `errors/` folder, never beside the code that throws it."
- `docs/conventions/naming.md` (lines 135-137): every `Error` subclass goes in a `*.errors.ts` file; "none is declared inline in a `service`, `routes` or other behavioural file."

Its sibling `MergeLockHeldError` already lives in `src/core/merge-gate.errors.ts`, and the service imports it from there at line 92. Some older files still declare error classes inline, such as `SlotWaitInterruptedError` and `HandoffMissingError`. They predate the rule, so they don't make a new one acceptable.

**Fix:** move the class and its JSDoc into `src/core/merge-gate.errors.ts`. Then point these imports at `./merge-gate.errors.js` (or `../core/merge-gate.errors.js` from `src/cli`):

- `merge-gate.service.ts`
- `src/cli/index.ts:68`
- `src/cli/index.test.ts:108` and `:197`
- `src/core/land.test.ts:44`
- `src/core/merge-gate.test.ts:122`

findings.description: An interrupt during the steer drops every peer already collected in `unsteered`, plus the peers still left, with no line printed. The land is recorded and a re-run refuses, so those sessions are named nowhere: the gap the new print-before-audit exists to close.

ADR 99's new unsteered paragraph says `pup land` "still exits as its audit says", but on a lost lock it exits 1 regardless of the audit (refuseScrubbed after printAuditOutcome), which ADR 88 in this same PR states; add "or 1 when the lock was lost (decision 88)".

The release-only identity pre-check now lives in the shared `dropMergeLock`, whose boolean `reclaimMergeLock` (line 770) ignores right after reading the same identity; the check belongs in `release()`, the only caller that needs it.
`release()`'s catch wraps `directoryIdentity` in a nested try/catch that maps any lstat error to "lost"; either say that rule in the existing comment or drop the inner try/catch.

The comments above the new lost-lock tests for `pup land` and `pup merge` ("Landed, and a re-run refuses it, but another run may have run alongside...") restate the production comments almost word for word; the test titles and assertions already carry them.
